description: Fix learning_interference benchmark to achieve std >= 0.10 across models
steps: Step 1: Read current task_interference.py in repo/benchmarks/learning/ and KNOWLEDGE entry on Learning Interference Scoring v2
Step 2: The v2 scoring fix was implemented but std=0.037 persists — diagnose why by running against 3 models (Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B) via run_benchmark_bedrock.py
Step 3: Increase difficulty spread: add harder interference conditions (more overlapping categories, longer lists, shorter retention intervals) and easier baseline conditions
Step 4: Re-run against 3 models, verify std >= 0.10 and range >= 0.20
Step 5: Update the corresponding notebook repo/notebooks/learning_interference.ipynb to match task file changes

description: Fix exec_func_wcst benchmark to achieve std >= 0.10 (currently std=0.007)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/executive_functions/task_wcst.py and the KNOWLEDGE entry on WCST single-trial being trivial

Step 2: Implement full 128-card Wisconsin Card Sorting Test protocol: present cards sequentially in a single prompt, require the model to sort by an unstated rule, shift rule after 10 consecutive correct without announcing the shift
Step 3: Score perseveration errors (continuing old rule after shift), categories completed, and total errors with weighted composite
Step 4: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target std >= 0.10
Step 5: Update notebook repo/notebooks/exec_func_wcst.ipynb to match
Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/executive_functions/task_tol.py to understand current Tower of London implementation
Step 2: Diagnose floor cause: likely output parsing failures, overly hard puzzles, or unclear instructions
Step 3: Add easier 2-move and 3-move problems alongside hard ones; create 3 difficulty tiers weighted 0.20/0.30/0.50
Step 4: Fix any answer parsing issues — verify model output format matches expected extraction regex
Step 5: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target mean >= 0.20 and std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update notebook repo/notebooks/exec_func_tol.ipynb to match

description: Fix social_cog_false_belief benchmark — ceiling effect at 0.967
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/social_cognition/task_false_belief.py
Step 2: Add 3rd-order and 4th-order nested belief scenarios (Alice thinks Bob thinks Carol believes...)
Step 3: Add false-belief scenarios with misleading surface cues that reward literal interpretation over mental state tracking
Step 4: Create 3 tiers: 1st-order (0.15 weight), 2nd-order (0.30 weight), 3rd/4th-order (0.55 weight)
Step 5: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target mean <= 0.85 and std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update notebook repo/notebooks/social_cog_false_belief.ipynb

description: Fix social_cog_pragmatic benchmark to achieve std >= 0.10 (currently std=0.036)
steps: Step 1: Read repo/benchmarks/social_cognition/task_pragmatic.py
Step 2: Add harder pragmatic inference items: indirect speech acts, conversational implicature requiring world knowledge, politeness-based indirection, Gricean maxim violations
Step 3: Add items where literal and pragmatic interpretations conflict sharply — understatement, litotes, rhetorical questions
Step 4: Create difficulty tiers: direct implicature (0.15), indirect/contextual (0.35), complex multi-layer (0.50)
Step 5: Test against Opus, Nova Pro, Ministral 3B — target std >= 0.10
Step 6: Update notebook repo/notebooks/social_cog_pragmatic.ipynb

description: Run all non-metacognition tracks against all 10 Bedrock models and compile results
steps: Step 1: Verify all benchmark fixes from prior tasks are in place (learning_interference, exec_func_wcst, exec_func_tol, social_cog_false_belief, social_cog_pragmatic)
Step 2: Run attention (4), learning (4), executive_functions (5), social_cognition (4) benchmarks against all 10 models using run_benchmark_bedrock.py with <=4 concurrent processes
Step 3: Compile results into repo/results/score_matrix_all_tracks.csv
Step 4: Generate per-track discriminatory analysis summaries in repo/results/ (mean, std, range per benchmark)

description: Draft writeups for attention, learning, executive functions, and social cognition tracks
steps: Step 1: Read repo/WRITEUP_METACOGNITION.md as the quality bar and template
Step 2: Read per-track results from repo/results/ (score matrices, discriminatory analyses)
Step 3: Draft repo/WRITEUP_ATTENTION.md — cite Posner 1980, Treisman and Gelade 1980, Wickens 2002; highlight divided/selective/sustained attention constructs
Step 4: Draft repo/WRITEUP_LEARNING.md — cite Thorndike 1932, Ausubel 1968; highlight transfer, interference, curriculum effects
Step 5: Draft repo/WRITEUP_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTIONS.md — cite Miyake 2000, Diamond 2013; highlight inhibition, shifting, updating constructs
Step 6: Draft repo/WRITEUP_SOCIAL_COGNITION.md — cite Baron-Cohen 1985, Grice 1975; highlight ToM, pragmatics, sarcasm constructs
Step 7: Each writeup must follow required template, be <= 1500 words, and include organizational affiliations section
Step 8: Generate cover images for all 4 tracks at repo/assets/{track}_cover.png — grouped bar charts similar to metacognition cover style
